thread:
sam: FYI — Dedicated customer on eu-west-1 reporting ~5x throughput drop starting ~10:12 UTC. Seeing API 429s and token-level tail latency spikes. @oliver @maya can you triage?
infra-bot: ALERT pool=eu-west-1-ded severity=warning queue_length=820 avg_batch_tokens=12 worker_util=0.32 autoscaler_events=0
oliver: on it. Any recent deploys or config changes? Which model and avg seq len?
sam: No deploys. Model=open-llama-13b, typical seq ~256 but traffic is very spiky with many tiny prompts. Customer says callbacks timed out.
maya: tiny prompts + continuous batching often yields tiny average batch tokens; scheduler might be preferring latency and not letting batches fill. Can you grab batch metrics?
eli: also paste the pool scheduler config and autoscaler settings.
sam: metrics dump from the pool exporter:
```
batch_size_p50: 6
batch_size_p90: 14
queue_time_ms_p90: 280
worker_util: 32%
requests_per_sec: 420
avg_tokens_per_request: 8
```
zoe: those numbers explain it — underfilled batches kill throughput. Worker util low so autoscaler didn't kick.
oliver: pulling pool config now. Found: min_replicas=2 max_replicas=8 scale_up_threshold=0.9 scheduler.policy=latency_prefer max_batch_tokens=1024 batch_fill_timeout_ms=8
maya: that explains it. With batch_fill_timeout_ms=8ms and latency_prefer, batches flush too quickly, so avg tokens stay small. Autoscaler threshold 0.9 also prevents scaling when util ~0.32.
eli: suggested mitigation: relax latency preference to allow larger fill, increase max_batch_tokens, and lower the scale_up_threshold so autoscaler scales on throughput signals.
maya: concrete quick changes I recommend: set `scheduler.policy=throughput_prefer`, `batch_fill_timeout_ms=50`, `max_batch_tokens=4096`, and `autoscaler.scale_up_threshold=0.6`. This should allow batches to accumulate and autoscaler to react earlier.
sam: customer wants repro steps so they can validate. Proposed stress script (small prompts flood):
```
# run from a small VM with token in env
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"open-llama-13b","input":"hi"}' &
  sleep 0.01
done
wait
```

sam: applied the quick patch to the pool: increased max_batch_tokens and batch_fill_timeout.
infra-bot: AUTOSCALER event pool=eu-west-1-ded from=2 to=5 reason=scale_up_threshold_breached metrics(util=0.62 avg_batch_tokens=48)
maya: observability shows avg_batch_size climbing from ~12 -> ~48 within 90s and queue_time_p90 dropping to ~60ms. Worker util up to ~0.62.
eli: watching logs, tail latency back to normal, 429 rate dropped to near zero.
zoe: i'll open an RFC to standardize these defaults for Dedicated pools and add a rollout checklist (targeting eng-infra + eng-runtime).
oliver: follow-up action — add an alert that fires when avg_batch_tokens < 20 AND worker_util < 0.5 AND queue_time_p90 > 200ms. This will catch the inefficient-batching pattern early.
maya: will add dashboard tile and alert. Also adding a note to the docs about tuning `batch_fill_timeout_ms` vs latency SLOs.
sam: Customer notified and we're continuing to monitor. Thanks all :thumbsup:
oliver: nice triage. If stable for 24h we'll close the escalation.
